# Spar 0.6.5

**The difficulty badge becomes a reading. The word on a problem now opens onto
what the problem is worth, where you stand against it, and how often someone at
your rating solves it — and the agent is held to that same window when it writes
a challenge rather than only when it fetches one.**

## What a problem is worth

- **The badge opens.** "Developing" was the only status-shaped thing on the
  header and the one thing that was not a number. The word stays and becomes the
  handle: hover it for the problem's rating, the basis that rating rests on, the
  concepts it trains and where you stand on each.
- **One number, three presentations.** The Spar Rating is an affine map of the
  underlying Glicko-2 estimate — same order, same sign, same history, no second
  scale. Codeforces is that estimate unchanged, because the estimate is run on
  that scale. LeetCode is the one real translation, anchored at the points where
  the two populations can actually be compared instead of the invented floors and
  ceilings it replaces.
- **The shown difficulty is the graded difficulty.** Pricing a challenge is one
  function now, `challengeItemRating`, and both the panel and the scorer call it.
  The number you read before you start is the number the result is scored
  against, by construction rather than by agreement.
- **It says what kind of fact it is.** A published Codeforces rating is a
  measurement, a band is a bucket hundreds of points wide, and a challenge Spar
  wrote is one author's judgement. The panel labels which, and quotes your chance
  in whole tenths — "about 6 in 10" — because a rating carrying a 150-point
  deviation does not support a decimal place.

## Challenges written at your level

- **Generated challenges get the level check sourced ones always had.** The
  asymmetry was not a decision: a fetched problem was measured against the
  training window while a challenge Spar wrote itself was whatever word the model
  felt like — which is how a learner rated 1635 ended up on a run of 1200-priced
  drills, solving every one, teaching the rating nothing, and staying provisional
  forever.
- **It refuses only when a better word exists, and it names that word.** Above
  roughly 2000 the window sits entirely above the top band, so the check stands
  down rather than becoming a gate nothing can pass. A refusal the agent cannot
  act on in one attempt is a refusal it works around.
- **A cold start stays a cold start.** Before anything has been graded the window
  is inverted out of a seeded rating nobody earned, so it does not get to overrule
  the pedagogy. One graded result is enough to turn it on.
- **The check runs before the compile,** not after it. A challenge pitched at the
  wrong learner is wrong whether or not it builds.

## The attempt the tutor read

- **`read_attempt` is drawn instead of dumped.** It was a single 16k line of
  escaped JSON with your solve log inside it — the worst payload in the app to
  meet as a payload, and the one with the most to show as itself.
- **Five views, because the replay answers five questions.** Cases read across
  the runs, runs read against the one before, the log reads in order, the code
  reads as code, timings read as the gaps you sat in. The tab that opens first is
  the one with something in it.
- **Built from the report, not the events.** The panel cannot show you more or
  less than the tutor actually saw, and a payload with no report in it falls back
  to the raw view rather than drawing an empty panel that claims the attempt was
  empty.

## Around the session

- **A way home in the stepper.** From challenge 2 of 13, getting back to the end
  of the session was eleven presses of the same arrow. The end of a session is a
  destination, not a direction, so it has its own control.
- **Ask about a specific challenge.** Attaching one to a message is a real
  attachment now — a pill on the composer that the turn is told about — rather
  than a prefix typed into your draft.
- **The stepper knows which challenge you are on.** Solving one does not
  immediately produce the next, and in that gap the trail called the challenge you
  were sitting in "Practice · not recorded" and stepping away and back opened the
  practice sandbox instead of the workspace.
- **Opening a question moves immediately.** The page owns its own read, so a
  successful click no longer looks inert while the session stays on screen.
- **Tracks can be deleted,** from the same ⋮ the sidebar's session rows use, with
  a confirmation that says how many sessions go with it.
- **Solved-attempt and system rows are drawn as rows** — a title, what happened,
  and the verdict tag — instead of a wall of orchestration prose.

## Fixes

- Leaving the challenge page no longer disposes Monaco models belonging to the
  workspace or to the editor's own attached model, which could blank the editor
  on the way in.
- The challenge stepper appears for single-challenge sessions, which previously
  had no trail at all.
